item.title: Live Music with Mitch Gregory at Cherry Crest Adventure Farm — Fri Oct 23, 6:00 PM — Cherry Crest Adventure Farm
item.description:
Check out our amazing lineup of musicians that will be performing live right here at the farm! Join us on select Friday evenings and Saturdays for toe-tapping tunes from our favorite bands. Mitch is a multi-instrumentalist playing guitar, slide guitar, the Wazinator, and is an accomplished harmonica player, and vocalist. Since the 80’s Mitch has performed through out Pennsylvania – Jazz, Blues and Rock collaborations in 2019, Mitch began entertaining as a solo performer. Mitch embarked on an eighteen month residency at the Boomerang/Harrisburg Comedy Zone focused on the blues and assembling material for his current project MITCH GREGORY BLUES. Mitch is performing Texas blues, New Orleans blues, Chicago blues, British and country blues in the styles of: Stevie Ray Vaughan, ZZ Top, BB King, Dr. John, Stray Cats, Rolling Stones, The music of Louis Jordan and much more.

item.description:

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: #475 In-Cab Experience at Strasburg Rail Road — Sat Oct 24 — Strasburg Rail Road
item.description:
***Starts October 24th & 25th 2026*** The Experience
Whether you choose to focus on the precision of the throttle or the rhythmic art of the shovel, you’ll be responsible for keeping a piece of history in motion.
Choose Your Role The Engineer: Take the throttle in hand. You’ll learn to manage the delicate balance of steam pressure and traction, feeling the raw power of the locomotive respond to your touch. Under the DSLE’s watchful eye, you’ll master the starts, the stops, and the subtle “talk” of the engine. The Fireman: The heart of the engine is the firebox, and you are its guardian. You’ll learn the technique of feeding the beast —maintaining the ideal fire bed and monitoring water levels to ensure the engineer has the power they need to tackle the line.

item.title: Inspired by Tarot: Grades 6-9 at PCA&D — Sat Oct 24, 12:30 PM — Pennsylvania College of Art & Design – Center for Creative Exploration
item.description:
Explore the symbolism and visual language found in the tarot! Tarot card reading is an ancient practice that people have used in analyzing and finding deep meaning. In this workshop, we will explore the history of the tarot deck and look at visual interpretations throughout history to the present. Students will then have the opportunity to create their own deck! We will talk about imagery, symbolism, and have a variety of mixed media options to make your deck come to life. Students are welcome to bring a deck along for inspiration! Expect a lot of creative freedom in this workshop!
Register Now
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Monster Parade – Digital Illustration Inspired by Collage: Grades 9-12 at PCA&D — Sat Oct 24, 1:00 PM — Pennsylvania College of Art & Design – Center for Creative Exploration
item.description:
Using Photoshop we will create new, never before seen creatures out of a variety of photos and simple painting techniques. Use your imagination and curiosity to combine various existing creatures and things into an endless parade of new and unique Monsters. Students will learn to use simple tools in Photoshop to simplify and process various types of images into unified collage base pieces. We will make selections, transform pieces, and merge them together into one unified layer before adding a little bit of highlight and even color. Photocredit: Sheri Hansen

item.title: Children's Chapel — Sun Oct 25, 10:30 AM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Oct 22, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

Along the way, your guides will share the historical facts about our buildings and the stories behind the folklore. It’s a walking tour for ages 16 and up that blends real history with the ghost stories passed down through generations – and you’ll come away knowing downtown Ephrata a little better, and maybe looking over your shoulder a little more.
